segments.source: Espresso evidence and its practical consequence
segments.context: Espresso assessment Espresso: fixed conditions shift the work to the grinder   8.8 out of 10   9Barista controls the water side of the recipe for you. The company specifies about 9 bar and 93°C, while the basket accepts 17–20 g and the collected output is normally around 40–45 g. That leaves coffee, dose, distribution and grind as the useful daily controls.This is not automatically limiting. A stable target can be liberating when you want a familiar espresso every morning. It becomes restrictive when a very light coffee asks for a different temperature, longer preinfusion or intentionally declining pressure.   Espresso evidence and its practical consequence   SignalWhat the evidence saysBuying consequence      Regulated brew stage 9Barista documents a mechanical twin-boiler system that reaches approximately 9 bar and controls brew water near 93°C.Treat it as an espresso brewer with a fixed operating point, not as a moka pot and not as a profiling machine.   53 mm basket The current Standard uses a 53 mm basket; Pro includes an IMS precision basket and naked portafilter.A capable espresso grinder and careful puck preparation remain essential even though the brewer regulates pressure.   Independent cup reports Tom’s Guide evaluated a Mk.2 Pro for roughly a month; Lance Hedrick demonstrated the Mk.2. Older Hoffmann, Bon Appétit and The Drive work covers the same core concept but not every Mk.2 revision.The evidence supports the concept, while generation labels should stay attached to any observation.   One output window The official target is approximately 40–45 g from a 17–20 g dose.Buy it for a compact double-espresso style result, not for one-touch singles, long drinks or freely selected brew ratios. segments.context: Classic Pro E24: the buying decision

segments.source: E24 updates the Classic's boiler material while keeping the compact manual format that defines the machine. The current North American version pairs a brass boiler with a 58 mm portafilter, nine-bar calibration, mechanical switches and a conventional steam wand. It gives a buyer a familiar accessory path and leaves room in the station budget for a grinder, but supplies no factory PID or shot timer to manage the routine. Brewing and steaming also use the same boiler in sequence. The attraction is a serviceable traditional platform whose owner wants to learn temperature timing and preparation, rather than an electronically guided first machine.
